proof.text: Prove the geometric assertions by induction on $j$. For $j=1$, $h_1=f_1$, $p_1^{(1)}=1_{X_1}$, and $X_1\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is the composite of $f_1$ and $B\to\operatorname{Spec}k$. Composition preserves separatedness by clause (e) of [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence] and finite type by clause (1) of [lem-sfb-finite-type-composition-base-change]. The identity is separated and of finite type directly from the definitions. Suppose the assertions hold at $j$. In the fibre-product square [def-pc-fibre-product], $a_j$ is the base change of $f_{j+1}$ along $h_j$, and $b_j$ is the base change of $h_j$ along $f_{j+1}$. Thus both projections are separated by [lem-weil-pbc-separated-base-change] and of finite type by clause (2) of [lem-sfb-finite-type-composition-base-change]. Now $h_{j+1}=h_j\circ a_j$, $p_i^{(j+1)}=p_i^{(j)}\circ a_j$ for $i\leq j$, and $p_{j+1}^{(j+1)}=b_j$. The same composition results give all the required properties, including that $P_{j+1}\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is separated of finite type. This proves the induction without imposing any flatness condition on the morphisms.

proof.text: Choose, for each of the finitely many $K_i$, a finite Tor interval $[u_i,v_i]$. All schemes and morphisms used below satisfy the geometric hypotheses by Step 1. For each fixed $j$ and $i\leq j$, [lem-sf-pullback-tor-amplitude] gives $E_i^{(j)}:=L(p_i^{(j)})^*K_i\in D^b_{ctf}(P_j,A)$ with the same interval $[u_i,v_i]$. Define the prefixes $Q_1=E_1^{(j)}$ and $Q_{s+1}=Q_s\otimes_A^L E_{s+1}^{(j)}$ for $1\leq s<j$. Induct on $s$: the initial assertion is the one just proved; clause (ii) of [lem-sf-tensor-ctf] gives $Q_{s+1}\in D^b_{ctf}(P_j,A)$ with interval $[\sum_{i\leq s+1}u_i,\sum_{i\leq s+1}v_i]$ from the analogous bound for $Q_s$. Hence $T_j=Q_j$ belongs to the claimed category for every $j$. For $j<r$, apply [lem-sf-pullback-tor-amplitude] once more, now to $(a_j,T_j)$ and $(b_j,K_{j+1})$, to obtain both individual pullback-domain assertions. In particular their tensor product also belongs to $D^b_{ctf}$ by [lem-sf-tensor-ctf]. The case $j=1$ involves a single factor, not an empty tensor. In Lean, ctf_of_iso transports the finite support and constructible homology along an isomorphism and composes each Tor-test representative with its inverse. For binary tensor closure choose representatives of both objects and a K-flat resolution of the first, apply lem-sf-tensor-ctf(ii), and transport through the native one-K-flat tensor comparison and the isomorphisms of the representatives. The prefix induction then uses these binary closure assertions.

proof.text: Fix $j<r$ and put $a=a_j$. Use [prop-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-ring-map] for the canonical isomorphisms $u^{-1}A_V\cong A_U$ for every scheme map $u:U\to V$ in this construction. The composite identification is compatible with them: both send every constant $c\in A$ to $c$, so the uniqueness of the constant-section-preserving identifications in that statement identifies them. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-derived-pullback-composition] applies with the required compatible coefficient sheaves. Distribute $La^*$ across a left-associated tensor of $s$ objects by induction on $s$. For $s=1$ take the identity. At $s+1$, first use the binary isomorphism of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback], then tensor the previously constructed $s$-factor isomorphism with the identity of the last factor. At $s=j$ this gives $La^*T_j\xrightarrow{\sim}\bigotimes_{i\leq j}La^*L(p_i^{(j)})^*K_i$. For each $i\leq j$, apply the inverse of $c_{a,p_i^{(j)}}$ from [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-derived-pullback-composition] and the identity $p_i^{(j+1)}=p_i^{(j)}\circ a$ to its factor. Tensoring these isomorphisms gives $\lambda_j:La^*T_j\xrightarrow{\sim}\bigotimes_{i\leq j}L(p_i^{(j+1)})^*K_i$. These are isomorphisms in the derived category itself, constructed from the canonical bifunctorial tensor comparison and the canonical composition components, rather than identifications only of cohomology sheaves.

Tensor lambda_j of Step 3 with the identity on the last pulled-back factor, using the tensor bifunctor of lem-sf-ringed-derived-native-tensor. The actual projection definitions say that the first j+1 coordinates are the composites through fst and the last coordinate is snd. Consequently the target is definitionally the next left-associated external product. The existing regroup definition gives this isomorphism; no associator or closed structure is needed. For one factor the tensor prefix is its only factor; when r=1 there is no next-product assertion.

title: Regrouping and finite-Tor domains of relative external powers
statement:
Use the finite-coefficient conventions [def-pur-conventions], with $A=A_{E,n}$. Let $B$ be a separated finite-type $k$-scheme, let $r\geq1$, and let $f_i:X_i\to B$ be separated finite-type morphisms with $K_i\in D^b_{ctf}(X_i,A)$ [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude], for $1\leq i\leq r$. Form left-iterated fibre products $P_1=X_1$ and $P_{j+1}=P_j\times_B X_{j+1}$ [def-pc-fibre-product], with structure maps $h_j:P_j\to B$ and projections $p_i^{(j)}:P_j\to X_i$. Put
$$T_j=\bigotimes_{i=1}^j L(p_i^{(j)})^*K_i.$$
For $j<r$ write $a_j:P_{j+1}\to P_j$ and $b_j:P_{j+1}\to X_{j+1}$ for the two projections. Then $P_j$ is separated of finite type over $k$, all $h_j,p_i^{(j)},a_j,b_j$ are separated of finite type, and $T_j\in D^b_{ctf}(P_j,A)$. Both $La_j^*T_j$ and $Lb_j^*K_{j+1}$ belong to $D^b_{ctf}(P_{j+1},A)$, and there is a canonical isomorphism in the derived category
$$\rho_j:La_j^*T_j\otimes_A^L Lb_j^*K_{j+1}\xrightarrow{\sim}T_{j+1}.$$
Here $\rho_j$ is the iterated derived tensor-pullback comparison [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback] followed by the pullback-composition comparisons [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-derived-pullback-composition] for $p_i^{(j+1)}=p_i^{(j)}a_j$ for $i\leq j$ and $p_{j+1}^{(j+1)}=b_j$, with the canonical tensor associators. No compact-support direct-image hypothesis, duality axiom or exceptional adjoint is part of the assertion.
